annotations.title: Natural disasters and warnings in a country, a region or the world

description:
Disasters, hazards and official warnings across a country, a region (bbox) or the whole world, most severe first by Criora Severity (severity_rank) beside the issuer's own level: wildfires, earthquakes, tsunamis, tropical cyclones, floods, eruptions, volcano alert levels, ash clouds, droughts, weather warnings and air quality.

Use for "what is happening in Japan", "which red warnings are in force in Europe", "the strongest earthquakes this week" (days 7), what happened in a country over recent days (days, up to 30). Near one place: get_hazards_near. A country holds an event by its point. For the whole world the answer opens with the Earth's pulse (earth_pulse), one figure for "how dangerous is the world today".

bbox.description: A region as [west, south, east, north] in degrees; across 180, give east past 180 ([120, -50, 300, 30])

country.description: Only events in this country or territory: its ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code (e.g. JPN, PRI) or its name

days.description: Every event active in the last N days, 1 to 30, each marked current or over; for this week, 7. Omitted, only what is current now, which drops most earthquakes a day to four days after they struck

event_types.description: Only these types of event; every type when omitted

kinds.description: Only occurrences, warnings or statuses; all of them when omitted

min_severity.description: Only events at least this severe; every severity when omitted

response_format.description: concise (default) answers the question; detailed adds every field the sources give

name: list_hazards

non_residential.description: Workplaces, shops, industry, services and their contents

total_high.description: The high end of the two's total

total_low.description: The low end of the two's total: its cost per square metre alone reads so

volcano_levels.description: Whether a volcano observatory's alert levels reach Criora there; false means a volcano is known only by its eruptions as reported, not by its standing level

warnings.description: Whether any official warnings feed covers it; false means no authority's warnings reach Criora there

last_read.description: When it was last read whole; null if never. Detailed only

status.description: silent: its last runs failed, since last_read

types.description: The hazards it reports. Detailed only

warnings.description: Whether it reports an authority's warnings rather than what is happening. Detailed only

attribution.description: The credit the licence asks for when it is retold

name.description: The feed's name as it is cited

driver.description: The event that weighs most in it now

level.description: very_low, low, medium, high or critical

meaning.description: What the scale's two ends stand for

people.description: People in the zone of events their issuers rate moderate or above

pulse_url.description: The page that explains the figure

strongest_30_days.description: The strongest event of the last 30 days

value.description: 0 to 100, read on a logarithm of the people within reach of events now

distance_km.description: From the event to the place

active_at.description: The latest moment the source reports it active

areas.description: Concise only: how many areas one warning covers, where its issuer files one for each

bounds.description: The area's box as [west, south, east, north], a bbox for list_hazards; east is below west across 180. Null for a record with no area. Detailed only

building_value.description: Replacement cost of the buildings and contents inside the footprint (GHS-BUILT-V 2025 priced by country), indicative and not market value; null until counted. Detailed only

confidence.description: confirmed (an authority, or two independent sources agree), single_source, preliminary (a first automatic solution, revised within the hour) or modelled (a forecast model's, never graded above medium for air quality)

current.description: Given only when days asks for past events: true while the event is still going on or in force, false for one that was active in those days and is over

expires_at.description: When the source says it ends; null when it states none

footprint.description: What drew the footprint people are counted in: area (the record's own), gdacs (GDACS's shape for the episode), shaking (the ground a quake shakes hard enough to damage buildings), detections, burned_area, vent, station

headline.description: What to tell first: a warning's headline as its issuer wrote it, else the event's label and where it is; the concise form gives it only where the issuer wrote one

issued_at.description: When the source issued this record

issuer_text.description: A warning's headline, description and instruction as the issuing service published them for the public, attributed to its sender. Null when the source gives none

kind.description: occurrence (something happening), warning (an authority's message about an area) or status (a standing state, such as a volcano's alert level raised above normal)

local_context.description: Where the event is, in words: its distance from the place that best locates it (the nearest town, or a bigger city a little further), and that place's population

metadata.description: What the source says beyond the value. A USGS earthquake carries depth_km, magnitude_type, felt_reports (Did You Feel It? reports), cdi and mmi (felt and ShakeMap intensity), pager_alert and review_status; an EMSC earthquake depth_km, magnitude_type, emsc_felt_reports (felt reports people sent EMSC), contributor (the agency whose solution it is) and region; a NOAA tsunami bulletin its centre, magnitude, origin_time and depth_km; an NHC or JTWC storm its max_wind_kt (1-minute), pressure_mb and movement, JTWC's also jtwc_warning (the warning's number), jtwc_synoptic_at, jtwc_position_accuracy_nm and jtwc_wind_radii_nm (the reach of 34, 50 and 64 kt winds); a JMA storm its max_wind_kt_10min (JMA's 10-minute wind, never converted) and typhoon_number; a MeteoAlarm warning its awareness_level (yellow, orange, red) and awareness_type; an Environment Canada alert its alert_type (warning, watch, advisory, statement), colour, impact, forecast_confidence and event_end_at. Detailed only

official_level.description: The issuer's own level in its words and scale: a CAP severity (Severe), a MeteoAlarm, GDACS or USGS PAGER colour, a hurricane category, an AQI category. Null where the issuer gives none; severity is the class of Criora's rank beside it

page_url.description: The event's own permanent page on Criora, for a major event, to cite

people.description: People living inside the footprint (GHS-POP 2025), for a quake those in shaking that damages buildings, fewer than GDACS's or PAGER's counts of who felt it; null until counted or where none is drawn

people_in_destructive_winds.description: A cyclone's people within GDACS's winds of 120 km/h or more, the figure for who a storm threatens; people is everyone in its wider footprint. Null for any other event, or where GDACS draws no such winds

place.description: The place that locates the event, the one local_context words

provenance.description: Each report the record holds: where it came from, who issued it and when; credit names its licence. Detailed only

received_at.description: Concise only: when Criora received the source's report

sender.description: The issuing authority, when the source relays many

severity.description: The class severity_rank falls in, critical, high, medium or low, which min_severity selects by

severity_rank.description: Criora Severity, 0 to 100, comparable across hazards and versioned (severity_version): the official level on a common scale, the people inside its footprint and the reading's place among its type's. The official level is never replaced by it

track.description: A moving event's positions, oldest first: kind observed where it was seen, forecast where the source expects it

trend.description: upcoming (a warning whose hazard has not begun; onset_at says when it does), new (first received within its kind's recent window; a status, set within it), intensifying or weakening (against the last day's readings, by severity and, where the value is the issuer's estimate, by value), steady, or ended; a quake is never intensifying or weakening

url.description: Concise only: the page of the report the record was read from, to cite

url_source.description: Concise only: whose report `url` is, where it is not `source`'s

why.description: What set the severity, ready to retell: the reading, the issuer's level, the people and where they were counted (a quake's in shaking that damages buildings, not everyone who felt it)

official_level.description: The issuer's own level, in its words

received_at.description: When Criora received this version of it; unknown for reports stored before 2026-10-18

source.description: The feed the report came through

url.description: The report's own page, where the source publishes one

Truncated.description: Set when an answer was held under its size: the tail of its main list left out.

field.description: The answer's list that was cut

left_out.description: How many of its entries, the least important, were left out

left_out_names.description: Each entry left out, where the list is not ordered by importance

why.description: The limit, and how to ask for the rest

counts_by_kind.description: Every match, as occurrence, warning or status

coverage.description: For a country, what reports there and whether each source is reporting now

credit.description: How a retelling credits the answer: Source: Criora with a link to the page the answer is about, then each originator whose data it quotes in the words its licence asks for. Concise, each credit once; detailed, by source with its name and licence, criora first

data.description: The highest severity_rank first, then the most recently active

data_as_of.description: When each quoted source's feed was last read whole, by source; a reading can be older than this when the feed has not changed. Null for a source never read

earth_pulse.description: For the whole world, one figure for the Earth now; null while it cannot be read

methodology_version.description: The methodology version the answer was made under

period.description: What the list covers in time: what is current now, or the last days asked

severity_version.description: The version of Criora Severity the ranks are

total.description: Every event that matched; data lists the first of them

truncated.description: Absent unless the answer was cut to fit

title: Natural disasters and warnings in a country, a region or the world
